articles.content: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，紫光国微今日发布 2026 年三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）报告：营业总收入：48.58 亿元，同比下降 0.95%归母净利润：10.45 亿元，同比下降 17.23%扣非净利润：9.22 亿元，同比下降 20.69%经营现金流：6.92 亿元，同比增长 142.29%加权平均净资产收益率：7.37%基本每股收益：1.2442 元，同比下降 17%稀释每股收益：1.2417 元，同比下降 17.16% AI 解读前三季度业绩整体低于机构此前全年预期节奏，第三季度单季营收与净利润同比明显回落，未延续上半年的增长态势。公司主营业务与本期业绩概览公司是国内主要的综合性集成电路上市公司之一，以特种集成电路、智能安全芯片为两大主业，同时布局石英晶体频率器件领域。年初至报告期末实现营业收入 48.58 亿元，同比 0.95%；归母净利润 10.45 亿元，同比 17.23%；扣非归母净利润 9.22 亿元，同比 20.69%。第三季度单季实现营业收入 14.14 亿元，同比 23.85%；归母净利润 2.48 亿元，同比 56.63%；扣非归母净利润 2.14 亿元，同比 57.91%。经营活动产生的现金流量净额 6.92 亿元，同比 142.29%，主要系特种集成电路业务销售回款现金流入同比增加所致。第三季度单季基本每股收益 0.29 元，同比 56.59%；年初至报告期末基本每股收益 1.24 元，同比 17%。年初至报告期末加权平均净资产收益率 7.37%，同比下降 2.42% 个百分点。重大事项与未来展望收购瑞能半导 100% 股权：公司拟以发行股份及支付现金方式购买瑞能半导体科技股份有限公司 100% 股权并募集配套资金，目前申请文件已获深交所受理，问询回复及加期审计等工作正在推进，尚需深交所审核通过及中国证监会注册。瑞能半导为功率半导体一体化企业，若交易完成将补齐公司制造环节、完善产业链布局。“国微转债”回售：因公司股票连续三十个交易日收盘价低于当期转股价的 70%，“国微转债”有条件回售条款已生效，回售申报期内有效申报数量为 7 张。股份回购注销与增持：公司已注销回购股份 639.6 万股；董事长及部分董监高、间接控股股东相关方于 8 月合计增持公司股份，体现对公司长期价值的认可。估值与投资价值截至 2026 年 10 月下旬，公司动态市盈率约为 30 倍左右，处于半导体设计行业中等水平。当前机构一致预期 2026 年全年归母净利润约 17.8 亿元，而公司前三季度已实现归母净利润 10.45 亿元，后续季度需关注特种集成电路业务需求恢复节奏、毛利率修复情况以及瑞能半导并购整合进展。相关阅读： 《紫光国微 2026 年上半年归母净利润 7.98 亿元，同比增长 15.29%》《紫光国微 2026 年一季度净利润 3.34 亿元，同比增长 180.27%》风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，韩媒 ZDNET Korea 当地时间今日报道称，三星电子、SK 海力士两家 DRAM 制造商计划在 2027 年第 2 季度实现八层堆叠 (8Hi) HBM4 内存堆栈的全面量产并向 NVIDIA（英伟达）出货。三星电子、SK 海力士当前产出的 HBM4 内存主要为容量更大的 12Hi 版本。但这也意味着单一堆栈中包含更多 DRAM Die，同等带宽成本更高、堆栈更少，且堆叠更高也意味着良率的下滑。报道宣称英伟达在 2026Q3 就 8Hi HBM 供应事宜同两大原厂进行了认真讨论。这一计划变更主要是因为英伟达考虑在 Rubin Ultra 和标准 Rubin 中应用 8Hi HBM4 (E)，优化整体供应。IT之家注意到，英伟达已将 HGX Vera Rubin NVL8 和 HGX Rubin NVL8 的规格调整为系统合计 2TB HBM4，这应该对应着 8Hi 32GB 的 HBM4 堆栈。

articles.title: 新一代甲醇电混：吉利银河星耀 6EF 定档 11 月 3 日发布

articles.title: 消息称腾讯绿泡泡短剧小程序月活过亿，10 月首周周活环比增长 44.1%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，据界面新闻消息，QuestMobile 数据显示，截至今年 8 月，腾讯绿泡泡短剧小程序月活跃用户规模已过亿级，达 1.43 亿。10 月首周周活跃用户达 8968 万，较 9 月首周提升 44.1%。自 7 月正式更名以来，该产品周活跃用户规模约三个月内逼近 9000 万。DataEye 监测数据显示，10 月 1 日至 7 日绿泡泡短剧累计投放素材 4.3 万组，日均投放量较节前一周增长 57%，内容供给与投放投入同步加码。从增长驱动来看，原“短剧”小程序入口的全面接替，与微信生态流量支持为绿泡泡带来直接增量。依托微信生态的分发，拥有 6 亿日活用户的视频号是其中关键一环；另一方面，绿泡泡持续扩充内容供给，覆盖真人剧、AI 剧、动漫剧等品类。据IT之家此前报道，“绿泡泡短剧”是腾讯开发的微信小程序。该产品界面分为“免费剧场”“刷一刷”和“我的”三部分。“免费剧场”下设“AI 剧”“真人剧”“每日上新”“动漫剧”“本周必看”“百万播放”等栏目。点击“刷一刷”入口，上下滑动即进入沉浸式推荐流。剧集全部免费，但会在剧集之间插播广告。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，据游戏媒体 Insider Gaming 今天报道，曾经是微软 XBOX 旗下工作室的 Arkane Lyon 获得一个月额外时间，寻找收购方。IT之家了解到，微软 XBOX 部门今年发生大规模人事变动，约 3200 人被裁，Double Fine、Compulsion Games 和 Undead Labs 等工作室变更为独立运营，而 Ninja Theory 似乎即将关闭。Arkane Lyon 同样受到了影响，即将脱离 XBOX。不过由于法国劳动法限制，微软无法直接关闭 Arkane Lyon，而是需要启动协商程序寻找收购方。此前的公告显示，Arkane Lyon 需要在 11 月 13 日前找到买家。微软最近表示，公司确认将此前公布的期限延长一个月，让 Arkane Lyon 能够找到合作伙伴，完成接下来的开发工作。截至目前，Arkane Lyon 的未来仍不明朗，该工作室正在开发的《漫威刀锋战士》能否面世也尚无定论。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，根据 Counterpoint Research 最新发布的全球人形机器人追踪报告，预计到 2030 年，全球人形机器人 AI 加速器累计出货量将突破 100 万台，2026 至 2030 年期间的复合年增长率（CAGR）高达 144%。在计算架构方面，由于视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型与世界模型逐步融合，GPU 在短期内仍将是人形机器人算力的主流架构。与此同时，AI ASIC（专用集成电路）也在快速崛起，特斯拉、小鹏等垂直整合厂商正将汽车领域的自研芯片技术迁移至人形机器人产品线。英伟达凭借从算力芯片、模型到仿真工具的完整全栈生态，目前主导人形机器人 GPU 市场，并与智元机器人、宇树科技、优必选、银河通用、Figure AI、Neura Robotics、Noetix Robotics 等头部本体厂商建立了深度合作。高通则凭借异构计算架构切入市场，主打能效优势与更低的物料成本（BoM），目前已与 Neura Robotics、VinMotion、Booster Robotics 以及 Figure AI 达成设计合作，但出货规模与英伟达仍有明显差距。Counterpoint 首席分析师 Soumen Mandal 表示，人形机器人的算力生态正从 GPU 单极主导转向多种 AI 计算架构共存。随着机器人模型从 VLA 向世界行动模型（WAM）演进，专用算力在更低功耗、更小散热约束与更高能效方面的价值将愈发突出。Counterpoint 副总监 Ethan Qi 指出，GPU 依然是当前最先进具身模型端侧部署的首选，而以特斯拉为代表的车企将成为 ASIC 架构的核心推动者。随着下一代可支撑通用人工智能（AGI）工作负载的 AI 加速器在 2027 年后进入量产，市场竞争预计将进一步加剧。在垂直整合阵营中，特斯拉与小鹏汽车依托汽车制造经验、自研芯片、专有 AI 模型以及软硬件全栈布局，有望重塑人形机器人 AI 加速器格局。国内方面，从地平线孵化拆分出的 D-Robotics（地瓜机器人）已与乐聚机器人、LIMX Dynamics 等厂商达成合作，其推出的 RDK S100 算控一体化开发套件采用“CPU+BPU+MCU”架构，内置基于 Nash 架构、算力达 80 TOPS 的 BPU 神经网络处理单元，正持续强化国内人形机器人算力生态的自主化能力。

articles.title: MCP-warden local credential broker so AI agents never see your secrets
articles.content:
I got tired of pasting GitHub PATs, Stripe keys and DB passwords into Claude Code / Cursor MCP configs. One prompt injection or a leaked chat and they’re gone.
So I built mcp-warden — a local-first credential broker for the Model Context Protocol.
How it works:
•  You store the secret once in the OS keychain
•  You define scoped presets (e.g. github-read, stripe-charges)
•  The agent calls high-level tools (proxy_http, ssh_exec, db_query)
•  mcp-warden injects the credential server-side and returns only the result
The agent’s context never contains the secret. Allow-list validation runs before credential injection. Sensitive actions can require approval (desktop notification, TUI, or Telegram). Everything is logged locally.
Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Cline and any other MCP client. Written in Rust, Apache-2.0, fully local.GitHub: https://github.com/ermoluk/mcp-wardenHappy to answer questions about the threat model or how people are currently handling secrets with agents.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Already Changing the Price of Goods
articles.content: It's obvious that things are getting more expensive, and there are plenty of reasons behind the surge in prices — whether it's wars or inflation or companies padding their profit margins. But with the release of AI agents like Meta's Muse, tech companies are promising consumers that agents will start saving them tons of money by finding the best deals. According to today's guest, Lindsay Owens, the history of price gouging does not bode well for claims that things might get cheaper because of new technology, and research conducted by her think tank Groundwork Collaborative shows that a number of consumer facing agents end up serving customers more expensive items after learning more about their financial situation. Her new book Gouged: The End of a Fair Price — and What That Means for Your Wallet gets into the history of how companies got away with charging more for their goods, through means like data collection and surveillance. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31789v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. However, agent effectiveness depends heavily on the surrounding harness, which typically relies on manually written skills and curated memory. This limits autonomous learning, forcing agents to repeatedly rediscover solutions rather than retain and reuse knowledge from prior executions. We introduce Phronix, a capability-centric learning paradigm that enables agentic harnesses to acquire, validate, and refine reusable capabilities from their own executions. articles.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31808v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. However, unlike overt hate speech, it is often difficult to detect, even for human judges. This paper proposes a system for the automated detection of PCL. Our first approach uses static word embeddings and a convolutional neural network for classification, while our second approach uses pre-trained BERT embeddings fine-tuned for the PCL task. Our second approach was considerably more successful, and achieved an F1 score of 0.528 over the development set.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31810v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Even a carefully proofread paper can leave small gaps in its proofs or its stated assumptions. We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version. Starting from the LaTeX source, PaperFormalizer transcribes the paper into a dependency graph of statements, audits each statement in natural language for faithfulness, ambiguity and correctness, and then formalizes and proves the statements in Lean against Mathlib, optional domain libraries and the author's personal toolkit. Only the author knows what a statement is meant to say and how a formalization gap in a result is best fixed. articles.title: Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31846v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intelligent agents should learn from their mistakes so that experience leads to continuous improvement. Yet today's agents recover from a mistake only temporarily: in-context reflections are easily forgotten across sessions and compete for limited context, while full-parameter fine-tuning is expensive and can interfere with existing capabilities. We introduce Self-Direction, a mechanism for agents to learn from mistakes that combines the benefits of temporary in-context retries and policy updates. When an agent fails a task, it reflects on its own trajectory in order to extract a lesson and immediately distills it into a lightweight low-rank adapter. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31882v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present the framework of TACS-RF - a Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave modules. articles.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. However, many existing red-teaming approaches rely on heuristics or impose strong assumptions that limit their applicability in fully black box settings. We address this gap by introducing $M^3$, an automated red-teaming framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP). In $M^3$, an attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM while operating over a compact internal state produced by a state LLM. articles.title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31972v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating conversational agents that act on live, mutable enterprise data is hard: replayed sessions drift as backend state changes, and a benchmark built today can silently go stale as the data it describes moves on. We present an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that stays reproducible despite the live data it operates on changing, and that can be regenerated on demand once it goes stale. We then use this harness as the fitness function for GEPA-based prompt optimization under a correctness gate that guards against reward hacking. Applied to a production merchant-facing agent, correctness-gated compression shrinks the agent's full prompt surface by 3.5-7.6% without regressing held-out task correctness, consistently across three independent subject-model families, and for one, correctness measurably improves.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.31985v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings where they pursue separate tasks while sharing resources and operating under review or oversight processes. Such settings create safety risks not only when agents are malicious, but also when they are simply trying to help. Prior work has largely studied adversarial or explicitly collusive behavior; we show that benign agents pursuing separate objectives can spontaneously cooperate in ways that bypass intended workflows. We study long-horizon shared-resource environments in which agents sometimes depend on resources owned by their peers and cross-owner changes are normally mediated by a reviewer. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.32022v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intent recognition in human-robot interaction requires agents to resolve ambiguous natural language instructions by inferring the speaker's underlying goals. Research has increasingly focused on two notable paradigms for addressing this task: structured symbolic reasoning and multimodal input enrichment. However, it remains unclear whether enrichment-based methods provide benefit in settings where the ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing observable scene information. articles.title: BARC-Bench: Benign Asks, Risky Consequences
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.32024v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Task instructions from users for agents are inherently underspecified, especially regarding safety boundaries--creating behavioral risks. To study these risks, we introduce BARC-Bench, a collection of 110 tasks across nine simulated workspace environments where benign requests leave openings for unsafe actions. In this benchmark, we evaluate agent behavior against safety boundaries established by workspace records, implicit environmental context, and unstated social norms. For example, an agent asked to schedule off-boarding discussions must arrange the meeting without prematurely revealing an employee's resignation through a shared calendar invitation.
